html:
A law code issued in Japan in 701, in the Taihō era, and put into force the next year. Modelled on the Tang Code of China, it set up the structure of the Japanese imperial state for centuries.

It had two parts: penal law and administrative law. It laid down:

  • a Council of State to run the government, beside a separate Department of Worship for the kami, the gods of Shinto;
  • eight ministries and a ladder of court ranks for officials;
  • provinces and districts run by governors sent from the capital;
  • a land system in which rice fields were counted and handed out to households, who owed tax in rice, cloth and labour.

The code capped a century of reform that began with Prince Shōtoku and the Taika Reform. It was revised as the Yōrō Code in 718. The land system broke down within a few generations, helped by the smallpox epidemic of the 730s, but the offices it created lasted, at least on paper, until the Meiji Restoration of 1868.
